thesis: Dollar General disclosed fiscal-Q2 net sales of $11.29 billion, up 5.2% year over year, and GAAP diluted EPS of $2.48 versus GAAP diluted EPS of $1.86 a year earlier, alongside a raised fiscal-2026 outlook. This suggests improving sales and earnings support a long thesis. The strongest counter-evidence is that tariff refunds contributed to the quarter and an active Dolgencorp case has an October 13, 2026 jury trial; those issues add nonrecurring-support and binary-event risk, but the broad category sales growth and higher same-basis GAAP earnings still leave a net positive read.
invalidation: Management reverses the raised fiscal-2026 outlook, sales growth weakens materially, or the October litigation event changes the operating or legal risk profile.

thesis: Affirm disclosed fiscal-Q4 revenue of $1.17 billion and fiscal-Q1 revenue guidance of $1.19 billion to $1.22 billion, which suggests company-specific operating momentum supports a long thesis. Consumer-credit and funding sensitivity are the strongest counter-evidence, while the broker news feed's per-share actual and estimate had unavailable accounting bases and therefore are not used as a beat comparison; the confirmed revenue result and forward revenue range still give a clear net positive read.
invalidation: Fiscal-Q1 revenue falls below company guidance, funding costs or credit losses worsen enough to erode revenue less transaction costs, or management cuts its forward outlook.

thesis: Nutanix disclosed fiscal-Q4 revenue of $757.1 million, up 16% year over year, ARR of $2.55 billion, up 16%, GAAP operating margin of 9.2% versus GAAP operating margin of 4.8% a year earlier, and free cash flow of $277.6 million versus $207.8 million. This suggests recurring growth, operating leverage, and cash generation support a long thesis. The strongest counter-evidence is a 120-basis-point decline in GAAP gross margin; it does not change the read because GAAP operating margin expanded 440 basis points and cash generation improved in the same disclosed quarter.
invalidation: ARR growth decelerates materially, fiscal-2027 revenue or free-cash-flow guidance is cut, or gross-margin compression persists without offsetting operating leverage.

thesis: SentinelOne disclosed fiscal-Q2 revenue growth of 21%, ARR growth of 22%, and raised fiscal-2027 revenue and adjusted/non-GAAP operating-income outlooks. The strongest counter-evidence is that GAAP gross margin fell to 72% from 75%, GAAP net-loss margin worsened to 32% from 30%, and the company's fiscal-2027 adjusted/non-GAAP EPS guidance is not comparable to its GAAP loss. These offsetting profitability signals leave the earnings evidence mixed despite strong growth, so the current read is to avoid a new position.
invalidation: Reconsider the avoid thesis if GAAP gross margin stabilizes and the GAAP net loss improves while ARR and revenue growth remain strong, or management raises forward outlook without widening losses.

thesis: HP disclosed fiscal-Q3 revenue growth of 12.5% and raised fiscal-2026 EPS and free-cash-flow outlooks; GAAP diluted EPS was $0.71, including an $0.11 tariff-refund benefit, and adjusted/non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.83, with the two bases kept separate. This suggests revenue growth and stronger cash-flow expectations support a long thesis. The strongest counter-evidence is that GAAP EPS declined 11.3% year over year, part of the quarter's support was nonrecurring, and an HP derivative-litigation settlement hearing is scheduled for September 18, 2026; those items add earnings-quality and binary-event risk but do not outweigh the raised outlook.
invalidation: HP cuts its fiscal-2026 outlook, memory and storage costs prevent margin stabilization, or the September litigation outcome adds a material liability or governance concern.
sources: In re HP Inc. Derivative Litigation order: https://case-law.vlex.com/vid/in-re-hp-derivative-1120457479
